From 1aec30021edd410b986c156f195f3d23959a9d11 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Li Chen <me@linux.beauty>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:26:16 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] ext4: publish jinode after initialization

ext4_inode_attach_jinode() publishes ei->jinode to concurrent users.
It used to set ei->jinode before jbd2_journal_init_jbd_inode(),
allowing a reader to observe a non-NULL jinode with i_vfs_inode
still unset.

The fast commit flush path can then pass this jinode to
jbd2_wait_inode_data(), which dereferences i_vfs_inode->i_mapping and
may crash.

Below is the crash I observe:

Fix this by initializing the jbd2_inode first.
Use smp_wmb() and WRITE_ONCE() to publish ei->jinode after
initialization. Readers use READ_ONCE() to fetch the pointer.

Fixes: a361293f5fede ("jbd2: Fix oops in jbd2_journal_file_inode()")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Li Chen <me@linux.beauty>
Reviewed-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260225082617.147957-1-me@linux.beauty
Signed-off-by: Theodore Ts'o <tytso@mit.edu>
Cc: stable@kernel.org

diff --git a/fs/ext4/fast_commit.c b/fs/ext4/fast_commit.c
index f575751f1cae..6e949c21842d 100644
--- a/fs/ext4/fast_commit.c
+++ b/fs/ext4/fast_commit.c
@@ -975,13 +975,13 @@ static int ext4_fc_flush_data(journal_t *journal)
 	int ret = 0;
 
 	list_for_each_entry(ei, &sbi->s_fc_q[FC_Q_MAIN], i_fc_list) {
-		ret = jbd2_submit_inode_data(journal, ei->jinode);
+		ret = jbd2_submit_inode_data(journal, READ_ONCE(ei->jinode));
 		if (ret)
 			return ret;
 	}
 
 	list_for_each_entry(ei, &sbi->s_fc_q[FC_Q_MAIN], i_fc_list) {
-		ret = jbd2_wait_inode_data(journal, ei->jinode);
+		ret = jbd2_wait_inode_data(journal, READ_ONCE(ei->jinode));
 		if (ret)
 			return ret;
 	}

diff --git a/fs/ext4/inode.c b/fs/ext4/inode.c
index 252191632f56..ac5f3446c731 100644
--- a/fs/ext4/inode.c
+++ b/fs/ext4/inode.c
@@ -128,6 +128,8 @@ void ext4_inode_csum_set(struct inode *inode, struct ext4_inode *raw,
 static inline int ext4_begin_ordered_truncate(struct inode *inode,
 					      loff_t new_size)
 {
+	struct jbd2_inode *jinode = READ_ONCE(EXT4_I(inode)->jinode);
+
 	trace_ext4_begin_ordered_truncate(inode, new_size);
 	/*
 	 * If jinode is zero, then we never opened the file for
@@ -135,10 +137,10 @@ static inline int ext4_begin_ordered_truncate(struct inode *inode,
 	 * jbd2_journal_begin_ordered_truncate() since there's no
 	 * outstanding writes we need to flush.
 	 */
-	if (!EXT4_I(inode)->jinode)
+	if (!jinode)
 		return 0;
 	return jbd2_journal_begin_ordered_truncate(EXT4_JOURNAL(inode),
-						   EXT4_I(inode)->jinode,
+						   jinode,
 						   new_size);
 }
 
@@ -4451,8 +4453,13 @@ int ext4_inode_attach_jinode(struct inode *inode)
 			spin_unlock(&inode->i_lock);
 			return -ENOMEM;
 		}
-		ei->jinode = jinode;
-		jbd2_journal_init_jbd_inode(ei->jinode, inode);
+		jbd2_journal_init_jbd_inode(jinode, inode);
+		/*
+		 * Publish ->jinode only after it is fully initialized so that
+		 * readers never observe a partially initialized jbd2_inode.
+		 */
+		smp_wmb();
+		WRITE_ONCE(ei->jinode, jinode);
 		jinode = NULL;
 	}
 	spin_unlock(&inode->i_lock);
--

The patch fixes a race condition where `ext4_inode_attach_jinode()` published a partially initialized `jbd2_inode`. The fast commit flush path could then read the non-NULL but incomplete jinode and crash when dereferencing `i_vfs_inode`. The fix ensures that the `jbd2_inode` is fully initialized before the pointer is made visible to other threads, using memory barriers and `READ_ONCE`/`WRITE_ONCE` for consistent ordering.

## Modifications by File

### `fs/ext4/fast_commit.c`
- **Modified `ext4_fc_flush_data()`**: Replaced direct access `ei->jinode` with `READ_ONCE(ei->jinode)` in both `jbd2_submit_inode_data()` and `jbd2_wait_inode_data()` calls. This ensures readers observe a fully initialized jinode due to the publication barrier in `ext4_inode_attach_jinode()`.

### `fs/ext4/inode.c`
- **Modified `ext4_begin_ordered_truncate()`**:
  - Added a local variable `jinode = READ_ONCE(EXT4_I(inode)->jinode)` to guarantee a properly ordered read of the pointer.
  - Replaced all references to `EXT4_I(inode)->jinode` with the local `jinode` to avoid the race.
- **Modified `ext4_inode_attach_jinode()`**:
  - Reordered initialization: `jbd2_journal_init_jbd_inode(jinode, inode)` is now called **before** publishing the pointer.
  - Added `smp_wmb()` and `WRITE_ONCE(ei->jinode, jinode)` to ensure that all initialization writes are visible to readers before the pointer becomes non-NULL.

## Relationship Between Changes
The core fix is the reordering and memory barrier in `ext4_inode_attach_jinode()`: the `jbd2_inode` (including its `i_vfs_inode` field) is fully initialized before publication. The `WRITE_ONCE` provides store visibility; `smp_wmb()` orders all preceding stores before the pointer store. The changes in `fast_commit.c` and `ext4_begin_ordered_truncate()` use `READ_ONCE` to ensure that loads of the jinode pointer see a consistent value respecting the barrier. Together, these modifications prevent any reader from obtaining a partially initialized jinode, eliminating the crash in the fast commit data flush path.

The patch fixes a race condition where `ei->jinode` was published (set to non-NULL) before the `jbd2_inode` structure was fully initialized. This caused concurrent readers (e.g., fast commit flush) to access a partially initialized `jbd2_inode`, leading to a crash when dereferencing `i_vfs_inode`.

### Modifications per file:

**`fs/ext4/inode.c`:**
- In `ext4_inode_attach_jinode()`: Reordered the initialization sequence to call `jbd2_journal_init_jbd_inode()` first, then use `smp_wmb()` and `WRITE_ONCE()` to publish `ei->jinode`. This ensures that readers who see a non-NULL pointer always see a fully initialized `jbd2_inode`.
- In `ext4_begin_ordered_truncate()`: Changed direct access `EXT4_I(inode)->jinode` to `READ_ONCE(EXT4_I(inode)->jinode)` to ensure the read observes the published pointer with proper ordering.

**`fs/ext4/fast_commit.c`:**
- In `ext4_fc_flush_data()`: Changed direct accesses `ei->jinode` to `READ_ONCE(ei->jinode)` in both `jbd2_submit_inode_data()` and `jbd2_wait_inode_data()` calls, ensuring the fast commit path only sees the fully initialized pointer and avoids stale/partial values.

### Relationships:
The changes form a symmetric fix: the producer side (in `ext4_inode_attach_jinode`) uses `smp_wmb()` + `WRITE_ONCE()` to guarantee that initialization completes before publication; the consumer sides (in `ext4_begin_ordered_truncate` and fast commit) use `READ_ONCE()` to ensure they see the fully initialized pointer with correct memory ordering. Together, they eliminate the race condition that caused the crash.

2.34.1

This patch fixes a concurrency bug where ext4 could expose a partially initialized `jbd2_inode` to concurrent readers, leading to a crash in the fast commit path. The fix ensures proper memory ordering when publishing the `jinode` field.

### Modifications in each file:

1. **`fs/ext4/fast_commit.c`**  
   - Changed `ext4_fc_flush_data()` to use `READ_ONCE()` when accessing `ei->jinode` in both `jbd2_submit_inode_data()` and `jbd2_wait_inode_data()` calls. This ensures readers observe a properly published pointer (or NULL) as per the ordering established by the writer.

2. **`fs/ext4/inode.c`**  
   - In `ext4_begin_ordered_truncate()`: Replaced direct access to `EXT4_I(inode)->jinode` with a local variable fetched via `READ_ONCE()`. This prevents reading a partially initialized pointer.  
   - In `ext4_inode_attach_jinode()`: Reordered the initialization sequence. Previously, `ei->jinode = jinode` was assigned before `jbd2_journal_init_jbd_inode()` completed. Now the jbd2_inode is fully initialized first, then a `smp_wmb()` memory barrier is placed before publishing the pointer with `WRITE_ONCE(ei->jinode, jinode)`. This guarantees that all writes to the `jbd2_inode` (including setting `i_vfs_inode`) are visible to other CPUs before the pointer becomes non-NULL.

### Relationships between changes:
- The reordering and memory barrier in `ext4_inode_attach_jinode()` (writer side) establish a happens-before relationship: any CPU reading `ei->jinode` via `READ_ONCE` (as done in `fast_commit.c` and `ext4_begin_ordered_truncate()`) will either see `NULL` or a fully initialized jbd2_inode. Without this ordering, readers could see a non-NULL pointer with uninitialized fields, causing a crash when dereferencing `i_vfs_inode->i_mapping` in the fast commit data wait path.
- Using `READ_ONCE` in the readers is necessary to ensure the compiler does not re-read the pointer and respects the writer’s memory ordering; it also prevents load tearing.

Here is the root cause:
In `ext4_inode_attach_jinode()` (fs/ext4/inode.c), the `ei->jinode` pointer was assigned before `jbd2_journal_init_jbd_inode()` fully initialized the `jbd2_inode` structure (specifically setting `i_vfs_inode`). This allowed concurrent readers in the fast commit path (fs/ext4/fast_commit.c) to observe a non-NULL `jinode` with an uninitialized `i_vfs_inode`, leading to a crash when dereferencing `i_vfs_inode->i_mapping`. The fix reorders the initialization to set `jinode` only after full initialization, using memory barriers and `READ_ONCE`/`WRITE_ONCE` to ensure proper visibility.

Here is the patch:
 
 static inline int ext4_begin_ordered_truncate(struct inode *inode,
 					      loff_t new_size)
 {
+	struct jbd2_inode *jinode = READ_ONCE(EXT4_I(inode)->jinode);
+
 	trace_ext4_begin_ordered_truncate(inode, new_size);
 	/*
 	 * If jinode is zero, then we never opened the file for
 	 * writing, so there's no need to call
 	 * jbd2_journal_begin_ordered_truncate() since there's no
 	 * outstanding writes we need to flush.
 	 */
-	if (!EXT4_I(inode)->jinode)
+	if (!jinode)
 		return 0;
 	return jbd2_journal_begin_ordered_truncate(EXT4_JOURNAL(inode),
-						   EXT4_I(inode)->jinode,
+						   jinode,
 						   new_size);
 }
 
 
 int ext4_inode_attach_jinode(struct inode *inode)
 {
 	struct ext4_inode_info *ei = EXT4_I(inode);
 	struct jbd2_inode *jinode;
 
 	if (ei->jinode || !EXT4_SB(inode->i_sb)->s_journal)
 		return 0;
 
 	jinode = jbd2_alloc_inode(GFP_KERNEL);
 	spin_lock(&inode->i_lock);
 	if (!ei->jinode) {
 		if (!jinode) {
 			spin_unlock(&inode->i_lock);
 			return -ENOMEM;
 		}
-		ei->jinode = jinode;
-		jbd2_journal_init_jbd_inode(ei->jinode, inode);
+		jbd2_journal_init_jbd_inode(jinode, inode);
+		/*
+		 * Publish ->jinode only after it is fully initialized so that
+		 * readers never observe a partially initialized jbd2_inode.
+		 */
+		smp_wmb();
+		WRITE_ONCE(ei->jinode, jinode);
 		jinode = NULL;
 	}
 	spin_unlock(&inode->i_lock);
 	if (unlikely(jinode != NULL))
 		jbd2_free_inode(jinode);
 	return 0;
 }
